absent: Meaning of start token value and predecessor lookup behavior beyond delegation.
Slab cache lifetime, flags semantics, and allocation failure modes beyond panic.
Sighand, pending queue, wait queue, and signal selection helper layouts and contracts.
Numeric user visible values for poll events, open flags, splice flags, message flags, and error codes.
Anonymous inode creation, fd installation, and compat mask conversion behavior.
Pipe ring, buffer, descriptor, and occupancy helper layouts and locking contracts.
Folio and page state helpers, LRU and gift and merge flag semantics.
Splice preparation, wakeup, direct execution, eof notification, and filesystem notify effects.

findings.text: Sequence list helper exposes head based RCU iteration start keyed by file offset, with zero meaning start marker and later offsets mapping to predecessor element lookup.
Sequence file subsystem provides boot time cache creation for its descriptor objects with accounting and panic on failure.
Signal file cleanup exposes wakeup of poll free waiters tied to sighand teardown.
Signal file private context holds a single signal mask selecting which pending signals the descriptor observes.
Signal file release frees its private context and always reports success.
Signal file poll registers interest on the sighand wait queue then under interrupt safe sighand protection reports readability when either private or shared pending sets intersect the selected mask.
Signal file poll and dequeue and mask update hold the sighand interrupt disabling spin protection while inspecting or changing pending sets and selected mask.
Signal file user record has fixed width of one hundred twenty eight bytes, zero padded with unused fields cleared.

Signal information translation selects output fields by abstract layout kind covering kill timer poll fault variants child real time and system call families, mapping process fault address trap machine check and timing values accordingly.

Signal dequeue operates either immediate with unavailable reported as retry, or waiting interruptibly with queue membership until a selected signal arrives or an unrelated thread signal aborts with restart.

Signal file read requires at least one full user record worth of destination space and moves as many whole records as fit, allowing the first wait to block then forcing later dequeues to be nonblocking, returning bytes moved or terminal error.
Signal file status display shows the complement of the internal selected mask under a sigmask label.
Signal file operations dispatch release poll vector read and no op seek, with optional status display when process filesystem support is present.

Signal descriptor creation and update validates creation flags, always excludes uncatchable termination and stop signals, stores the inverted user mask, creates anonymous file on new request or atomically replaces mask and wakes waiters on reuse with type check.
Signal file creation flags reuse the standard close on exec and nonblock numeric values.
Native and compat signal file system calls validate user mask size, copy the mask from user space, then delegate to shared creation logic with zero flags for legacy forms.
Pipe nowait clearing drops the nowait mode bit with an atomic compare exchange retry that tolerates concurrent mode changes.
Page cache pipe release returns the held page reference and clears the least recently used marker.
Page cache pipe confirmation treats already current contents as success and otherwise locks the backing folio to detect truncation with no data versus disk read failure with input output error.

Pipe buffer operation tables combine confirm release get and optional steal hooks, with page cache providing confirm, user page and default providing steal variants, and no steal variant omitting steal.
User page steal only proceeds for gifted buffers, marking least recently used before delegating to generic steal logic.

Splice into pipe transfers whole page descriptors from caller array into free ring slots, signalling broken pipe when no readers exist, reporting retry when no progress is possible, and releasing unconsumed source pages.
Single buffer pipe append fails with broken pipe signal when readerless and with retry when full, releasing the supplied buffer on either failure and advancing head on success.
Splice descriptor page arrays stay inline up to default pipe capacity and are dynamically allocated and freed only beyond that threshold, sized from current maximum usage.

Pipe to file and pipe to socket and pipe to pipe paths hold pipe mutex protection across ring inspection transfer and tail movement, with dual pipe transfer ordering locks by address to avoid deadlock.

Pipe to file splice requires file vector write support, confirms buffers while skipping empty ones, issues bounded vector writes, consumes fully written buffers and adjusts partial ones, wakes producers when space frees, and prefers bytes moved over trailing errors.
Pipe to file splice warns if a file write reports more than the prepared vector length, indicating overrun by the destination.

Pipe to socket splice waits for readable data while writers remain, aborts promptly on thread signals or nonblock request, maps splice more and file nonblock into message behavior, sends bounded page vectors, then consumes acknowledged bytes and wakes writers.
Splice from pipe to file requires destination splice write support and otherwise reports unsupported destination.
Direct splice actors bracket file splice with write section handling for direct path versus plain delegation for range path, with optional end of splice notification hook.
File range splice asserts an active write section on the destination and caps transfer length to the maximum read write count.
Write section check passes unconditionally for non regular files and otherwise reflects freeze write state of the hosting superblock.

General splice validates read and write modes, rejects offsets on pipe ends, forbids self splice and append destinations, checks pread pwrite capability for explicit offsets, verifies access ranges, propagates nonblock, updates implicit or explicit positions, and emits modify then access notifications on success.

Pipe to pipe splice moves whole buffers when the remaining length covers them and otherwise shares a prefix with gift and merge markers stripped, breaking on reader loss or completion and waking readers and writers as appropriate.
Pipe to pipe transfer retries preparation when racing with peer readers or writers yields no progress, holding both locks only while buffers move and releasing before waiting.
Truncated or unhashed folio during pipe confirmation yields no data which callers treat as end of available input rather than hard failure, risking short or empty transfers.
Splice to absent readers sends broken pipe signal to the caller in addition to returning pipe error.
